close_pull-request: Use for "close PR N in repo X without merging" closing the PR, and see reopen_pull-request to reopen a closed unmerged PR.
create_organization-repository: Use for 'create a repo called X in org Y' or 'make a private repo under my org' requests. It returns the created repository record. For listing repos already in the org, use list_organization-repository.
create_pull-request: Use for "open/create a PR from branch X into branch Y in repo R with title and body" creating the PR, and see edit_pull-request for changing its title, body, or base after creation.
create_release: Ask to create a release in a repo with a tag name, target commitish, name, notes, and draft or prerelease flags, and it creates that release, while get_repository-release owns viewing it.
dispatch_workflow: Ask to manually run a workflow_dispatch workflow by file name on a ref in a repo, and it triggers that workflow, while list_action-run owns the resulting run.
edit_pull-request: Use for "change the title/body/base branch of PR N in repo X" editing only those fields, and see close_pull-request for closing the PR without merge.
edit_release: Ask to edit a release by numeric id in a repo, and it updates its name, notes body, draft, or prerelease flags, while get_repository-release owns the current release values.
edit_repository: Ask to update description, website, default branch, issue flag, or PR flag for a coilyco or coilysiren repo. Use get_repository to read current metadata before editing.
get_action-run: Ask for a specific Actions run by run_id in a repo, and it returns its workflow, status, conclusion, commit, and timing, while list_action-run-job owns the jobs inside that run.
get_commit-status: Ask whether a commit SHA or branch in a repo is passing or failing, and it returns the combined overall CI state plus its statuses, while list_commit-status owns the individual entries.
get_organization: Use for 'tell me about org X' or 'is org X public' questions. It returns full name, description, website, and visibility. For the org's members use list_organization-member.
get_pull-request: Use for "what is PR N in repo X?" and "is PR N mergeable or merged?" returning the PR fields, and see get_pull-request-file for the files that PR touches.
get_pull-request-commit: Use for "what commits are in PR N in repo X?" and "show the commit list for PR N" returning paged commits in the PR, and see get_pull-request-file for changed files.
get_pull-request-file: Use for "what files changed in PR N in repo X?" and "how many additions and deletions in each file for PR N?" returning paged file changes, and see get_pull-request-commit for the commit list.
get_repository: Ask for repo metadata, default branch, topics, stars, or enabled features for a coilyco or coilysiren repo. Use edit_repository to change description, website, default branch, has_issues, or has_pull_requests.
get_repository-branch: Ask about a branch by name, whether it exists, its head commit, or its protection flag in a coilyco or coilysiren repo. Use list_repository-branch for all branch heads.
get_repository-content: Ask for one file by path, file content at a branch, or directory entries in a coilyco or coilysiren repo. Use list_repository-content for top level root entries.
get_repository-release: Ask for a release by tag name in a repo, and it returns its name, notes, assets, draft and prerelease flags, while list_repository-release owns listing releases.
list_action-run: Ask to list workflow runs in a repo and filter by event or status, and it returns Forgejo Actions runs newest first, while get_action-run owns the details of one run by id.
list_action-run-job: Ask what jobs are inside a specific Actions run by run_id, and it returns each job with its status and no logs, while get_action-run owns the run's workflow and conclusion.
list_commit-status: Ask what statuses exist on a commit SHA, branch, or tag in a repo, and it returns each individual CI status entry with context, state, and description, while get_commit-status owns the combined overall state.
list_current-user-organization: Use for 'what orgs does the bot belong to' questions. It returns the bot account's organizations. For a named user's organizations use list_user-organization.
list_organization: Use for 'what organizations exist on this server' questions. It returns all organizations. For orgs belonging to the bot account, use list_current-user-organization.
list_organization-member: Use for 'who belongs to org X' questions. It returns the members of one org. For org profile details like description or website use get_organization.
list_organization-repository: Use for 'what repos are in org X' or 'does org X own repo Y' questions. It returns repos owned by the named org. For repos owned by a user account, use list_user-repository.
list_pull-request: Use for "what are the open/closed/all PRs in repo X?" plus filters for labels, milestone, poster, and sort, returning PR summaries, and see get_pull-request for one PR's details.
list_repository: Use for 'what repos can the bot see' or 'list all accessible repos' requests. It returns bot-visible repos across all owners with ordering. For name or topic search use search_repository.
list_repository-branch: Ask what branches exist in a repo, list branch heads for a coilyco org repo, or show branches for a coilysiren repo. Use get_repository-branch for one branch by name.
list_repository-commit: Ask for recent commits, commits on a branch or SHA, or commits touching a file path in a coilyco or coilysiren repo. Use list_repository-tree to find files by name or extension.
list_repository-content: Ask for root files and folders at a branch or SHA in a coilyco or coilysiren repo. Use get_repository-content for one path.
list_repository-label: Ask which issue or PR labels are defined on a coilyco or coilysiren repo. Use get_repository for repo metadata and enabled features.
list_repository-release: Ask to list releases in a repo and filter by draft, prerelease, or name, and it returns releases newest first, while get_repository-release owns a single release by tag name.
list_repository-tag: Ask to list git tags in a repo and it returns the tags with their commits, while list_repository-release owns releases.
list_repository-tree: Ask for the git tree at a branch or SHA, every file path recursively, or find files by name or extension in a coilyco or coilysiren repo. Use get_repository-content to read a found path.
list_user-organization: Use for 'what orgs does user X belong to' questions. It returns orgs for the named user. For the bot account's org memberships use list_current-user-organization.
list_user-repository: Use for 'what repos does user X own' questions. It returns repos owned by one user account. For repos owned by an org, use list_organization-repository.
mcp_beaver_info: Report this MCP server's identity, mode, and served tool inventory. Read-only, reaches no upstream, and doubles as a liveness probe now that the protocol ping is gone.
merge_pull-request: Use for "merge PR N in repo X" plus optional style, title, message, or delete branch after merge, merging the PR, and see close_pull-request to close without merging.
reopen_pull-request: Use for "reopen closed PR N in repo X" reopening only closed unmerged PRs, and see close_pull-request to close it again without merge.
search_repository: Use for 'find repos named X' or 'does owner have repo Y' questions. It returns matching repos by name and metadata only, never file contents. For topic name search, use search_topic.
search_topic: Use for 'what topics exist for X' or 'how many repos use topic Y' questions. It returns topic names and counts, not the repos. For repos matching a topic use search_repository.
